claims.text: Uniformly dispersed nano-oxide particles in ODS tungsten alloys pin dislocations.
Dislocation pinning by nano-oxide particles impedes dislocation climb at high temperatures.
Impeded dislocation climb delays the onset of high-temperature plastic deformation.
An optimized nano-oxide dispersion improves toughness relative to conventional tungsten alloys lacking such a dispersion.
Y2O3 is a suitable nano-scale oxide for producing the proposed ODS tungsten microstructure.
The intervention is intended to produce a uniform oxide-particle dispersion both along grain boundaries and within grains.
Uniformly distributed nano-oxides act as dislocation-pinning sites.
Dislocation climb is thermally activated at high temperature.
Competition between thermal activation and oxide-particle pinning governs the onset of plastic strain.
Competition between thermal activation and oxide-particle pinning governs energy-dissipation processes that contribute to toughness.
Optimized ODS tungsten will have a higher yield point than the conventional tungsten baseline at 1200–1500 °C.
Optimized ODS tungsten will have greater toughness than the conventional tungsten baseline at 1200–1500 °C.
A suboptimal oxide dispersion will produce a more abrupt increase in plastic strain rate.
A suboptimal oxide dispersion will reduce toughness relative to an optimized dispersion.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply at 1200–1500 °C in inert atmospheres when dislocation climb is the dominant deformation mechanism.
The proposed mechanism is limited to material systems in which powder metallurgy can control nano-oxide distribution.
Achieving and confirming a uniform nano-oxide dispersion is experimentally challenging.
